assumptions: you use a published attack corpus rather than only your own fixtures
you link the repo and the CI run, or the number is decoration
clone_cost.estimate: 2 days for a Rust validator with a fixture generator and a CI matrix
clone_cost.why: the engine is small and the harness is standard cargo plus actions; the expensive part is sourcing real payloads, which this project did not do

hazard_note_absent: Security tooling that claims to catch drift. A missed vector is invisible by construction in a self-authored matrix, so publish coverage limits whenever you reuse this pattern.

prior_art.relation: same author's same platform - this page is one component of it, which is why the records are merged
runtime guardrails plus auditability for agents, delivered as middleware instead of a validator
compliance fleet that leans on vendor guardrails - same 'policy as code' instinct, less proof

what_breaks_first: A suite whose cases and fixtures are both authored by the system measures agreement with itself, so '12 of 12' says nothing about the attack space it did not write; and the pass claim is not reachable at all here - no repository, workflow URL or run id is linked. The honest next step for a clone is an external corpus of real malicious samples with a published miss rate.
what_to_steal: gen_fixtures.rs as a test *generator*: emit the clean and adversarial cases from the same spec the validator consumes, then let CI rebuild the whole matrix on every commit. It makes a regression impossible to hide and costs one file.
worth_note: The part worth keeping is the smallest credible security demo there is: a fixture generator plus a fixed scenario matrix wired into CI, so the artifact is a run rather than a slide. It is merged into the sibling submission because both pages describe one platform by one author, and the split version publishes twice the entries for half the evidence.
